_what: Close-out ledger rows whose §3 entry carries FLAGGED FOR DAVID but which DELIBERATELY have no block in docs/open-questions.md, each with the reason. Asserted by scripts/verify-register-blocks.mjs.
_the_rule_being_declared_against: CLAUDE.md §3b: a close-out that adds a FLAGGED FOR DAVID item adds a line to the register too — that is what survives the N=3 rotation. §3 rotates at N=3 and docs/handoff-archive.md is not loaded at session open, so the register is the only surface a question survives on.
_why_this_cap_exists: On 2026-09-15 the #331 and #333 blocks vanished in a merge conflict resolution, four days after the register was built, and nothing said a word. Ledger #339.
_two_kinds: Rows filed BEFORE the register existed (ece2d1a, 2026-09-11 18:25) are history the register never covered. Rows filed AFTER it are questions that were LOST, and the cap prints them on every run (it keys on ids above #302, the row that built the register) so that writing them down does not make them quiet.
_derived_not_transcribed: The ids came from the cap itself, run with an empty list. Each date and commit is the first commit that wrote the row, from `git log -S` on the ledger; each 'Work' is the row's own headline. One row (#249) was written in a merge commit, which `git log -S` skips unless given `-m`; it was dated by hand from that merge.
_this_list_prunes_itself: A declaration is STALE, and fails the build, if its id has no ledger row, if no entry claiming it carries FLAGGED FOR DAVID, or if the register has gained a block for it. Tech-debt #73.
